standard_prerequisites.name: The projection formula identifying the pullback of a pushforward along the fibre square
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter spaces-cohomology.tex, label lemma-affine-base-change (invoked at proof line 2036)
standard_prerequisites.use: Applied to the cartesian square with the two projections $p$ and $q$, it gives $f^*f_*\mathcal{F} = q_*p^*\mathcal{F}$, which is the sheaf whose relation to $\mathcal{F}$ is being described.

standard_prerequisites.name: The diagonal of a separated etale morphism is an open and closed immersion
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Standard: $\Delta : X \to X \times_Y X$ is an open immersion because $f$ is etale and a closed immersion because $f$ is separated (used at proof lines 2038-2039)
standard_prerequisites.use: It splits the structure sheaf of the fibre square into the diagonal and the complementary open and closed piece, which is what makes $p^*\mathcal{F}$ decompose.

core_obligations: Form the cartesian square with the two projections and identify $f^*f_*\mathcal{F}$ with $q_*p^*\mathcal{F}$ using the affine base change statement (proof lines 2029-2037).

Use that the diagonal is an open and closed immersion, since $f$ is etale and separated, to write $p^*\mathcal{F}$ as a direct sum of $\Delta_*\mathcal{F}$ and a quasi-coherent module supported on the complement of $\Delta(X)$ (proof lines 2038-2042).

Conclude the splitting: the composite $\mathcal{F} \to f^*f_*\mathcal{F} \to \mathcal{F}$ displayed by the author is the identity map, which the author verifies by tracing the maps through the decomposition (proof lines 2043-2049).
proof_roadmap: The cartesian square and the identification $f^*f_*\mathcal{F} = q_*p^*\mathcal{F}$ (proof lines 2029-2037).
The open and closed diagonal and the resulting decomposition (proof lines 2038-2042).
The composite is the identity (proof lines 2043-2049).
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that for a quasi-compact separated etale morphism the counit $f^*f_*\mathcal{F} \to \mathcal{F}$ admits a splitting (statement lines 2021-2026). The proof pulls the pushforward back along the fibre square, uses the fact that the diagonal is at the same time an open and a closed immersion to decompose the pulled back module into the contribution of the diagonal and a module supported on its complement, and then reads off that the resulting composite is the identity; the author displays the composite and leaves the tracing of the maps to the reader. The decomposition along the diagonal is the substance, so the claim is H2.
